title: Iceberg 1.13 release (Java)
summary: After 1.12 closed, Anoop (anoopj) opened the discussion on 1.13, proposing a release before the end of the year that includes early V4 work, and volunteered as release manager. Anurag Mantripragada had already volunteered for 1.13, so Anoop agreed to take 1.14. Anurag suggested early January because of the holiday season, with the V4 spec PR, related early work and Spark 4.2 support on his wish list; Russell Spitzer and Neelesh Salian also saw December as difficult. Dan (danielcweeks) said it is too early to rule out a release by year end, since releases need not be large. Xin Huang proposed that Spark 4.2 support cover existing Iceberg functionality, with new Spark features such as the Transactional API as best effort. No date or scope was settled.

positions.stance: Get another release out before the end of the year with some early V4 work, and he volunteers as release manager.
A December release is usually difficult, and Anurag, who already volunteered, should coordinate 1.13.
He will manage 1.13 and suggests early January, with the V4 spec PR, related early work and Spark 4.2 support in scope.
If 1.13 includes Spark 4.2, it should support existing Iceberg functionality and treat integration with new Spark features such as the Transactional API as best effort.
It is too early to discount a release by the end of the year; not every release needs to be large and several things missed the 1.12 cutoff.
The Spark 4.2 items in the tracking issue should be completed before deciding whether 1.13 or another release supports Spark 4.2.

outcome.note: Anurag Mantripragada is release manager for 1.13 and anoopj will take 1.14. The release date (end of year or early January) and the Spark 4.2 scope were not settled.

why_it_matters: It names the release managers for 1.13 and 1.14 and the candidate scope for 1.13: early V4 work and Spark 4.2 support.
